intervention_label: High-resolution HLA class I typing (HLA-A*02:01 / A*24:02) + HA-1/HA-2 minor-antigen genotyping of patient and sibling donor — diagnostic gate
expected_benefit: Resolves the allele-level HLA-A*02:01 (and A*24:02) status and the recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch that gate every HLA-restricted cellular lever this case was submitted to surface.
key_risks: None from the test itself; the risk is decision delay if the ~2020 typing report cannot be retrieved and typing must be repeated
HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is not a common catalog assay — may route as a send-out or through ALLOHA (NCT05473910) trial screening
Donor consent and a fresh donor sample are required for the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch call
preference_alignment: Directly serves the user's stated priority (de-risking the HLA-restricted immunotherapy pathway); matches 'prefers_trials' by opening the ALLOHA and Fred Hutch enrollment routes. No toxicity veto or modality constraint touches it.
guideline_status: Standard-of-care characterization before HLA-restricted cellular therapy; ELN 2022 and NCCN AML v3.2026 assume molecular/HLA workup precedes trial enrollment.
rationale_summary: Every persona converged here without reservation because the workup is non-toxic and it gates the entire HLA-restricted axis that motivated the referral. HLA-A*02:01 is the master switch for HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T (TSC-100/101, Bleakley HA-1 TCR-T, BSB-1001), WT1-C4 and PRAME-directed cells; A*24:02 opens the WT1-siTCR fallback if A*02:01 is negative. HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of both the patient and the HLA-identical sibling donor is a separate essential gate, since HLA-identical siblings can still differ at these minor loci. Pull the allele-level ~2020 transplant/donor-registry typing first and repeat high-resolution typing only if it cannot be confirmed. Until this returns, the rank-3 HA-1 TCR-T rec is unscoped and cannot be called deliverable. Retrieval is fast (3-7 days for HLA typing; 1-3 weeks for the send-out HA genotyping).
open_questions: If A*02:01 is negative, is A*24:02 positive (opens the WT1-siTCR fallback)?
Does the HA-1(H) recipient-positive / donor-negative mismatch actually exist once both parties are genotyped?
Can the allele-level 2020 typing be retrieved, or is a fresh draw needed?
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic gate, not a therapy — resolves the allele status and MiHA mismatch that determine whether any HLA-restricted lever is even enrollable.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic test on blood / archival typing record)
overall: The master switch for this run: every HLA-restricted immunotherapy option is stranded until allele-level typing and HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and donor return.

intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab) anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning + second allo-HCT (HCT2 platform)
expected_benefit: SIERRA (randomized phase 3, n=153): durable CR (>=180 days) 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) with 131I-apamistamab conditioning versus 0% (0-4.7) on conventional care, p<0.0001; EFS HR 0.23 (95% CI 0.15-0.34).
key_risks: Grade 3+ treatment-related AEs 59.7% versus 59.2% on conventional care — essentially no incremental burden as conditioning, but transplant-conditioning cytopenias, infection and mucositis apply
Second-transplant treatment-related mortality is uncharacterized: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients
No organ-function or cardiac labs on file yet; conditioning ahead of HCT2 needs that clearance first
preference_alignment: Matches curative intent and the efficacy-leaning weight (0.75); no modality ruled out — HCT2 explicitly acceptable, travel included; matches 'prefers_trials' via NCT07157514. The 0.75 weight should be revisited once fitness is known.
guideline_status: NCCN AML v3.2026 and ELN 2022 both keep second allo-HCT + clinical-trial enrollment in play for relapsed disease; Iomab-B enters through the category-2A clinical-trial route, not a drug-level category.
rationale_summary: All five personas endorsed this as the curative backbone: it is the one randomized phase 3 in the dossier that speaks to the actual problem, carrying an 85%-blast marrow into a transplant chemotherapy can no longer clear. The conservative and concensusite lead with it on evidence tier and guideline fit; the risktaker and advocate rank it just below their stated-priority immunotherapy because it is the platform on which HA-1 consolidation would be delivered. The load-bearing gaps are indirectness (SIERRA studied first transplants, so prior-HCT eligibility is untested) and the surrogate endpoint (durable CR, not OS — ITT OS was flat at HR 0.99, diluted by 52% crossover to the radioconjugate). The critic held it at moderate on those grounds without dissenting. Fitness and organ-function workup, flagged across the board as the master unknown, must land before conditioning. NCT02665065 is closed; the go-forward NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting.
open_questions: Does the go-forward conditioning trial (NCT07157514) admit prior-allo-HCT patients?
Is the patient transplant-fit? No cardiac, renal, or hepatic data on file.
Second-transplant TRM in a prior-allo-HCT relapse is not characterized by SIERRA.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate: the only randomized signal in the dossier (SIERRA dCR 17.1% vs 0%, p<0.0001), but read indirectly onto a prior-HCT relapse it did not enroll.
toxicity_burden: High (grade 3+ TRAEs 59.7%, at parity with conventional care — conditioning cytopenias, infection, mucositis; second-transplant TRM uncharacterized)

counter_productive_moa.description: Radioconjugate marrow injury could compromise engraftment if the HCT2 platform is not secured; no persona raised a mechanism objection.

overall: The curative backbone all five personas endorsed — the randomized way to carry active disease into HCT2, gated on a fitness workup that has not yet been done.

intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform; TSC-100 / BSB-1001)
expected_benefit: Krakow 2024 (single-arm phase 1, n=9): CR achieved or maintained in 4 of 9 post-allo-HCT relapses, with one patient in remission beyond two years; zero DLTs, zero CRS, zero ICANS.
key_risks: Lymphodepletion-related grade 3-4 neutropenia and grade 3-5 infection (Legionella, S. aureus pneumonia reported)
Two cases of mild grade 1-2 acute GVHD, attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal rather than the TCR-T
An 85%-blast marrow may outpace TCR-T kinetics; needs cytoreduction and the HCT2 platform in place first
preference_alignment: This is the explicit reason the case was submitted — the HLA-restricted immunotherapy priority, satisfied. Matches 'prefers_trials' (three recruiting slots: NCT05473910, NCT03326921, NCT06704152), curative intent, and the efficacy-leaning weight with no tolerability trade (0 CRS/ICANS).
guideline_status: No NCCN drug-level category; guideline-aligned through NCCN AML v3.2026's category-2A clinical-trial-enrollment route. ELN 2022 keeps adoptive cellular approaches open for post-transplant relapse but offers no DLI-vs-HCT2-vs-cellular sequencing consensus.
rationale_summary: Four personas ranked this; the advocate and risktaker led with it because it is the lever the referral asked to surface, and the concensusite ranked it via the trial-enrollment route. The critic ranked it too but refused to read the 4-of-9 CR as efficacy: n=9 is a single-arm feasibility cohort with no comparator, so response cannot be separated from lymphodepletion or clonal course. That evidence-quality caution is real but not biomarker-contingent — it persists in the positive branch. What confirmation does lift is the eligibility veto space: the conservative declined to rank it on evidence tier yet explicitly did not veto, noting the clean safety read. Everything here is conditional on HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, both pending; a negative test forecloses this rec entirely. The lineage-restricted mechanism keeps killing in the blood compartment, which is why the safety signal is so clean.
open_questions: Does the rank-1 workup confirm HLA-A*02:01 and the HA-1(H) recipient-positive / donor-negative mismatch?
If A*02:01 is negative but A*24:02 positive, the A*24:02 WT1-siTCR fallback (TBI-1301, n=8, transient responses) is the door that stays open — not ranked here as it is a negative-branch lever.
Can adequate cytoreduction and an HCT2 platform be delivered fast enough against an 85%-blast marrow for TCR-T consolidation to bite?
likelihood_of_effect: Assuming A*02:01 + HA-1 mismatch confirm: uncertain but curative-intent — 4/9 CR in Krakow 2024 (n=9 feasibility, no comparator). Negative typing forecloses it entirely.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (lymphodepletion neutropenia, grade 3-5 infection; mild grade 1-2 GVHD; no CRS, no ICANS across 9 patients)

counter_productive_moa.description: TCR-T kinetics may lag an 85%-blast marrow and antigen-loss escape is possible, but lineage-restricted killing limits off-target collateral.

overall: The only lever that answers the referral's own question — a clean-safety, curative-intent graft-versus-leukemia consolidation, live only if the pending typing confirms and delivered after HCT2.
scenario_label: If HLA-A*02:01 confirmed (allele-level) with a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch

expected_benefit: Pemmaraju 2019 (open-label single-arm phase 2, BPDCN): first-line CR/clinical CR 72% (21/29) at 12 ug/kg — but this is BPDCN, not AML, so the number is cross-tumor read-across, not indication data.
key_risks: Capillary leak syndrome (19%, boxed warning) with one death reported in each dose subgroup
Hepatic transaminase elevation (ALT 64%, AST 60% any grade) and hypoalbuminemia (55%) — the wrong toxicities to invite with undocumented organ function
Needs baseline albumin and cardiac/hepatic workup before it is safe to start
preference_alignment: CD123 is a user-named handle; the efficacy-leaning weight supports CD123 cytoreduction. Matches 'prefers_trials' via NCT06561152. No toxicity was vetoed, but the capillary-leak risk is a fitness gate given the missing organ-function data.
guideline_status: FDA-approved in BPDCN only; no NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing. For this AML marrow it is off-label cross-tumor read-across.
rationale_summary: Only the conservative ranked this, and chose it over pivekimab and flotetuzumab specifically for its worked-out capillary-leak management algorithm — the one CD123 option with an FDA label and ~8 years of post-marketing safety data. Both the critic and concensusite filed qualified cautions rather than dissents: the 72% CR is a first-line BPDCN result that does not transfer to an 85%-blast AML marrow, and the agent has no AML guideline standing. Those caveats are why this sits as considered-with-caveats despite no formal dissent — presenting an off-label cross-tumor agent as unqualified standard care would misstate its footing. It targets a confirmed feature (CD123 by flow), so it is not biomarker-gated, but quantitative CD123 antigen density is still pending and predicts benefit. Capillary leak with reported deaths makes the missing organ-function labs a hard prerequisite here too.
open_questions: Quantitative CD123 antigen density (ABC/MESF) is pending and predicts CD123-directed benefit.
Baseline albumin, cardiac and hepatic reserve are undocumented — required before capillary-leak-risk therapy.
Does BPDCN response translate to a high-burden AML marrow at all? No AML efficacy data exist for this agent.
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-uncertain for AML: headline 72% CR is first-line BPDCN cross-tumor (Pemmaraju 2019); no AML efficacy data and CD123 density still pending.
toxicity_burden: High (capillary leak syndrome with treatment-related deaths, transaminitis ALT 64% / AST 60%, hypoalbuminemia 55%)

counter_productive_moa.description: No clear mechanistic antagonism; the efficacy risk is cross-tumor non-transfer from BPDCN, not a counter-productive vector against the goal.

overall: The only labeled CD123 agent with a real safety algorithm, but its headline efficacy is BPDCN cross-tumor and its capillary-leak deaths demand organ-function labs first.

expected_benefit: Sievers 2001 (single-arm, first-relapse CD33+ AML, n=142): CR/CRp 30%. But the Hills IPD meta-analysis (n=3325, tier 1a) found no survival benefit in the adverse-cytogenetics stratum: OR 0.99 (95% CI 0.83-1.18) — this patient's exact complex/TP53-aberrant subgroup.
key_risks: Grade 3+ hyperbilirubinemia 23% and transaminase elevation 17% — hepatic and veno-occlusive-disease risk that compounds with a planned HCT2
Single-agent depth is modest (30% CR/CRp) and came from a cleaner first-relapse population, not this FLAG-IDA/venetoclax-refractory state with extramedullary disease
VOD is the characteristic class risk ahead of transplant
preference_alignment: CD33 is a user-named handle and the agent is FDA-approved on-label for R/R CD33+ AML. But the advocate dissented that spending a slot here inverts the user's stated immunotherapy priority given the null benefit in this stratum, and the 0.75 efficacy weight argues against it.
guideline_status: NCCN AML v3.2026 category 2A for relapsed/refractory CD33+ AML — but the pivotal ALFA-0701 RCT (RoB2:Low) is front-line de novo with benefit concentrated in favourable/intermediate cytogenetics, so the 2A listing does the work the trial population does not.
rationale_summary: The conservative and concensusite ranked this as the one agent that is both FDA-approved and guideline-listed against a target the patient carries. The risktaker and advocate dissented, and the tier-1a evidence backs them: the Hills meta shows OR 0.99 for survival in adverse cytogenetics, meaning zero signal in exactly this complex, TP53-aberrant karyotype. The critic, who ranked neither, made the same point independently — the strongest CD33 evidence in the dossier argues against use here, not for it. So a guideline listing and expected benefit part ways in this subpopulation. The hepatic and VOD load is also the wrong toxicity to invite right before a second transplant. It targets a confirmed feature (CD33), so it is not biomarker-gated, but quantitative CD33 density and the rs12459419 splicing genotype would temper or support it.
open_questions: Quantitative CD33 antigen density (ABC/MESF) and the rs12459419 CC-vs-CT/TT genotype both refine the ADC benefit prediction and are pending.
Would a fractionated 3 mg/m2 schedule (fewer early deaths, Hills) be used if it is pursued at all?
likelihood_of_effect: Low for this stratum: tier-1a Hills meta shows OR 0.99 (95% CI 0.83-1.18) — no survival benefit in adverse cytogenetics, the patient's exact subgroup.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (grade 3+ hyperbilirubinemia 23%, transaminitis 17%, veno-occlusive-disease class risk ahead of HCT2)

counter_productive_moa.description: P-glycoprotein efflux of the calicheamicin payload in adverse-karyotype blasts blunts CD33-ADC delivery — the subgroup where its own data show no benefit.

overall: The on-label, guideline-listed CD33 handle whose own tier-1a evidence shows no survival benefit in this complex/TP53-aberrant karyotype — familiar, but pointed the wrong way.

expected_benefit: Daver 2024 (phase 1/2, R/R AML, RP2D n=29): ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% (95% CI 6-36) — real single-agent CD123-ADC activity, not cross-tumor read-across. Kovtun 2018 preclinical: low-picomolar killing below the dose affecting normal progenitors.
key_risks: Dose-limiting reversible veno-occlusive disease at higher doses (0.180 and 0.450 mg/kg) — the basis of the conservative's veto ahead of HCT2
One treatment-related death reported across schedule A (0.300 mg/kg cohort, cause unknown)
At the RP2D: grade 3+ febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion reactions 7%, anaemia 7%
preference_alignment: CD123 is a user-named handle, the trial route (NCT03386513) matches 'prefers_trials', and the efficacy weight supports debulking. But toxicity_vetoes being empty does not neutralize a documented VOD signal — the conservative treats it as a hard safety gate, not a soft note.
guideline_status: Investigational; no NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing. Trial-enrollment route only.
rationale_summary: The risktaker and advocate both ranked this as a debulking bridge — the CD123 ADC with its own R/R AML numbers (ORR 21%) rather than borrowed BPDCN data, to knock down the 85% blast load ahead of cellular and transplant consolidation. The conservative vetoed it on toxicity grounds: a documented veno-occlusive-disease signal ahead of HCT2 in a patient with no baseline bilirubin, transaminases, or hepatic read on file. That veto is explicitly conditional and liftable — 'produce that clearance and I drop the veto' — but the condition is unmet, because organ-function labs are the case's flagged open item and do not exist yet. I am not overriding a live veto whose lifting condition has not been met: the row stays as not_recommended so the reader sees exactly what was considered and why it is currently gated, not silently dropped. It reinstates as a rankable debulking option the moment hepatic and albumin baselines clear it. Quantitative CD123 density is also pending and predicts ADC benefit.
open_questions: The veto lifts on documented baseline bilirubin, transaminases and a hepatic read — none currently on file.
Quantitative CD123 antigen density (ABC/MESF) is pending and predicts ADC benefit.
Is single-agent depth (ORR 21%) enough to meaningfully debulk an 85%-blast marrow, or is it a combination component?
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate as debulking: own R/R AML data (ORR 21%, 95% CI 8-40; cCR 17%), but single-agent depth is modest against an 85%-blast marrow.
toxicity_burden: High (veno-occlusive disease at higher doses, one treatment-related death; RP2D: febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion reactions 7%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Veno-occlusive disease from the ADC ahead of HCT2 could sink the very transplant the debulking is meant to enable.

overall: The CD123 ADC with the best own-disease data, held under a live, conditional VOD veto — it reinstates as a debulking bridge the moment hepatic and albumin baselines clear it.

expected_benefit: Uy 2021 (phase 1/2, primary-refractory/early-relapse R/R AML, RP2D n=30): CR/CRh 26.7%, ORR 30%. Vadakekolathu 2020 correlative substudy: 7 of 15 TP53-abnormal R/R patients reached under 5% marrow blasts.
key_risks: Cytokine release syndrome / infusion reactions are the class risk (largely grade 1-2 with step-up dosing, dexamethasone and tocilizumab)
Autologous T-cell fitness in a heavily pretreated post-transplant, FLAG-IDA/venetoclax-refractory marrow is unknown
No open enrollment route: MacroGenics deprioritized the program (NCT02152956 closed)
preference_alignment: CD123 is a user-named handle and the mechanism is on target, but there is no enrollable slot, which collides with 'prefers_trials'. The TP53-inflamed-marrow rationale would appeal to the efficacy-leaning weight if the program were open and the TP53 status confirmed.
guideline_status: No NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing; program deprioritized. Off-guideline mechanism evidence, not an open route.
rationale_summary: Only the risktaker ranked this, and openly as mechanism evidence rather than an enrollable option: TP53-aberrant AML runs an inflamed, IFN-gamma-high marrow, and on the flotetuzumab trial 7 of 15 TP53-abnormal patients dropped under 5% blasts. The critic dissented that this figure comes from Vadakekolathu 2020, an unadjusted post-hoc correlative subgroup where responders were the high-inflammation patients — a hypothesis, not an effect estimate. The concensusite dissented on guideline grounds: no listing, program shelved, closed trial. Both objections persist regardless of biomarker status. The honest read is that flotetuzumab-the-drug is not a route; the CD123xCD3 mechanism it validates is the reason to chase an open construct (a recruiting CD123xCD3 bispecific or a dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T), and to weigh the TP53-inflamed-marrow rationale only if TP53 confirms aberrant. It targets a confirmed feature (CD123), so it is not biomarker-gated on HLA.
open_questions: Is there an open CD123xCD3 or dual CD33/CD123 construct that carries the same mechanism into an enrollable trial?
Does the patient's TP53 status confirm aberrant, which is what the inflamed-marrow rationale rests on?
Is autologous T-cell fitness adequate after prior transplant and FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure?
likelihood_of_effect: Uncertain and not enrollable: 30% ORR in refractory AML (Uy 2021), TP53 signal from a post-hoc correlative subgroup (Vadakekolathu 2020); program discontinued.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (cytokine release syndrome / infusion reactions, largely grade 1-2 with step-up dosing, dexamethasone, tocilizumab)

counter_productive_moa.description: CD123xCD3 redirection needs fit autologous T cells; exhaustion after transplant and FLAG-IDA may blunt it, and the TP53 rationale is post-hoc.

overall: A discontinued drug carrying a live mechanism signal — its TP53-inflamed-marrow rationale is post-hoc, and the reason to chase an open CD123xCD3 construct rather than this one.
